judged_text: remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) then group.save and returns success_json even when the user was never a member, and group.save is a no-op on an unchanged record so validation cannot report the miss. A request with a stale or wrong user_id gets a 200 success while no membership was removed; the admin UI (which reloads the list and trusts the response) treats the no-op as a confirmed removal, hiding the real state from the operator.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then unconditionally returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds (which it likely will even if nothing changed). There is no check that a membership actually existed/was removed, so a wrong/stale `user_id` can yield 200 despite no removal. However, DELETE endpoints are often intentionally idempotent, and the client reloads members via `findMembers()` after the request, so it won’t necessarily “hide” real state; the core issue is lack of explicit feedback, not a verifiable functional break.
